[b]An end to the restorationists, an end to the war[/b]
The restorationist movement had, until this point, survived better than the isolationists. They had lived past the isolationist collapse at the hands of QASIC, but now it seemed that the isolationists were soon to suffer the same fate.

Relentless attacks had been carried out by the army and navy of Kuhaw-Astan, which had cost the restorationists much of northern Astanir. They were now cornered in the mainland between the peoples republic and the tribal republic.

Indeed, the military council could sense their imminent defeat, so they would take the only logic course of action for them, albeit a cowardly one. An overnight helicopter ride to the stronghold island would first allow the three council members; General Akuini / General Saloa / General Loni, safety from the mainland conflict. From there, they split up to avoid easy targeting from their many allies. Akuini would settle in [nation]Italian Dutch[/nation], whereas Loni would travel further to [nation]pantagruel[/nation] and Saloa would take off for a new life in Elseyr.

With the command structure of the restorationists now collapsed, their mainland territory would be free game for the two republics. Desertion rates would skyrocket as daily airlifts and boat trips took swathes of troops away to the stronghold island, where many would pursue the same fate as the military council. In the stronghold island, the most optimistic would stay behind to defend the island, but a coordinated naval invasion from either QASIC or kuhaw-Astan wound result in an easy victory and the acquisition of thousands of military and humanitarian supplies stored across the island.

A peace plan would arise between the two remaining sides of the conflict offering a split between the Astaniran territories. Kuhaw-Astan would accept and await the peoples republics response

Peace map: https://i.postimg.cc/NGTYCgk6/astan.png

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60807673][nation]Mizrahel[/nation]
[/quote]
[spoiler=[b]International Columns[/b]]
[b]International Columns of the Erenian Red Army[/b]

For the first time in its modern history, the Socialist International was under attack. Yet, the Presidium of the Socialist International was apprehensive about what manner of tone to undertake in reaction to this blatant slight. The Mizraheli nation was a growing fascist power, and yet what is their objective? Those on the far-left of the International's political scene exclaimed that the war was an intraimperialist war, fought between fascists on one side and former imperialists on the other. Thyven had yet to fully transition into a dictatorship of the proletariat, and the various liberal democratic mechanisms in the People's Congresses continue to persist even now.

It was even doubtful that a communist party could be formed at the moment which could stretch over the entirety of the nation. Therefore, who are we to defend imperialists against imperialists? Let their wars be fought and their people destroyed, and from the ashes will come a communist revolution.

However, these voices would be immediately silenced by the Presidium of the International. Argo Lo Pilato, the chief theoretician of the Democratic tendency within the International, would reason out that the Thyvenic state was already on the long road to revolution, that its state institutions were in a slow, transitional state devoted to the liberation of all workers and the destruction of the bourgeois, and that despite its immense conservatism, it has striven hard to obey various memoranda set forth by the International to guide it towards the upright path.

In a keynote speech defending the Thyvenic Revolution, Lo Pilato argued before the plenary session that [i]"... It is in our interests to accept the formation of a popular front against the enemy, to be constituted by all tendencies of the left and center, if it means we may survive another day against the parasitism of the right."[/i] and that [i]"... we simply wish to arm the whole masses, proletarian or bourgeois, to defend against those that seek to destroy our very way of life."[/i]

The other opinions of the plenary session would be summarized as follows:

[list]

[u]Graci[/u]: "Any comments made lamenting on the slow reforms of the Thyvenic state is made in dogmatism and rejection of socialism's adaptive nature; we cannot presume for the Thyvenic nation what the best practices shall be for them, it is for their revolutionary vanguard to sort out, which is presently in danger. The war in West Shamat is for many things. Nationality, religion, geopolitical stakes, money. Above all these things is power. Mizrahel, in committing its terrible war, seeks power over another nation so that the Jewish nation becomes synonymous with the Mizraheli nation. Therefore, the war in West Shamat is being committed so that the identity of one nation is completely and utterly dissolved by another. Shall good men watch as the world becomes darker?"

[u]Evesti[/u]: "We say that the Mizrahelis seek the destruction of communism while the Ma'arav do not. The distinction is deeper than this. Communism is the affirmation of liberty, whereas anti-communism is its negation. The Ma'arav have sided with the communist movement because it is a democratic body of soviets that seek the liberation of the proletariat, and as we deliberate in this plenary session, the forces of the far-right are now marching against the body politic of the free."

[u]Cui[/u]: "Many resources have been expended to vanquish the Astaniran fascists. Now this Presidium is demanding that more resources be spent, more lives be tossed away, for a distant war in the name of a nation that continues, continues, continues to defy our demands to institute democratic centralism and revolutionary vanguardism. This is an intraimperialist war between fascists and social fascists, and whatever victor exists shall result in the diminishing of the world revolution. If the Presidium's objective is to facilitate the exportation of the revolution, it can do so without getting involved in nonsensical, impractical, and neurotic misadventures in Shamat."

[u]Terrasi[/u]: "Thyvenic markets were on a positive trend up until the outbreak of this war. If things continue on as they are, collectivization of key Thyvenic industries may be delayed, which will in turn cause the whole state to fall behind schedule on the International's requested reforms. Somare S.p.A. and Almstedt Corporation are particularly concerned that rising costs in living combined with political uncertainties may lead many Thyvenic citizens to seek out more profitable labor markets, particularly in Norrhollow and Hyperion. If the International wants to intervene, it's best to do it now, or not at all."

[u]Benir[/u]: "The Astaniran Section of the International follows the opinion of the Qianxun section and believe that this is an intraimperialist war. Military resources that might be expended in Mizrahel will be best used instead to help stabilize the People's Republic of Astanir and the Commonwealth of Gythena against their respective counterrevolutionary movements."

[/list]

In total, this would come out to two opposed against four in favor (Including Lo Pilato), leading to further debates to determine the best course of action. After several more deliberations, the Socialist International would vote unanimously in favor of protecting the Thyvenic state from Mizraheli aggression and would organize the formation of two institutions:

First, all national armed forces of all member states would be proclaimed subsections of a greater institution known as the "Erenian Red Army (ERA)", which was to be the first instrument of global revolution. On paper, the ERA was meant to be a world army, representing the interests of all communist parties. In practice, however, the ERA would be more of a unified command structure than a truly unified armed force, hearkening to the successful operations of QASIC during the Astaniran Civil War. 

Second, a volunter force known as the "International Columns" would be established to operate under the Erenian Army, to be composed not of army regulars but communist volunteers, whom the Socialist International would empower to participate in all conflicts deemed to be geopolitically necessary for the triumph of communism over capitalism. Though nominally a decentralized structure, the command hierarchy of the International Columns would be monopolized by Qianxun military officers, who would also spearhead recruitment efforts from fifteen participating political parties.

The exact breakdown of volunteers from these parties would be as follow:

Volunteers would be flown into Thyven on flights paid for by the Socialist International, who would also pledge to shoulder the costs of arming and training these volunteers for the war in Ma'arav. Though, with most volunteers being veterans of the war in Sal-Baliz, Sikirsk, and now Astanir, the International Columns would be considered fairly reputable especially when compared with the largely unproven armed forces of both Thyven and Mizrahel.

Eduard Moncur de Waal, the Gythenan People's Commissar for War, would be invited by the Presidium to take control of the International Columns in recognition of his decent track record in tense urban warfare, which will be necessary for the war in West Shamat. After some deliberation, Moncur de Waal would agree and would be sent together with various Astaniran and Qianxun military advisors to Thyven as Supreme Commander of the International Columns of the Erenian Red Army.

Deliberation would also begin on sending military equipment to Thyven in support of its war effort. However, due to logistical uncertainties, these would be held off for now.
[/spoiler]

[b]The purpose of war[/b], by Argo Lo Pilato

It is an interesting thing when a holistic ideology is confronted by a narrow-minded one, especially so when the critic seeks to be paradoxically within the field of geopolitics and yet also outside of it. Here is an Islamic middle power, without any particularly strong ties beyond its regionalist core of allied powers, that repeats the same mistakes made by the Socialist International during the formulation of its First Conference of Discussions: That the enemy of fascism is itself an enemy.

But interestingly enough, the conventions are reversed. In the First Conference, the Presidium condemned any notions of alliance with the liberal center and the social democrats as a pitfall into "right opportunism". That is, the surrender of the worker's revolution to bourgeois democracy. Now we see the same with the Baladullahans, who accept the evils of ethnofascism but condemn the struggle of those being aggressed upon, as though in the contest between two powers, the fate of all happiness rests with the comfortable middle ground.

War is hell. Many times, we see the phrase muttered, whether in genuine contempt by the men in the arena or as passive platitudes of comfortable outsiders. But hell is a headlong descent, and beneath war is the moral degradation of the chauvinists who think that peace is the supreme master of war. Certainly, I disagree with those who deem war horrible even at the moment of greatest necessity.

The Baladullahans do not understand the purposes of war, for they do not understand the urgency of the worker's revolution. They think so little of war because they believe there can be no war raised by people to safeguard against fascist aggression. In their minds, so long as these good men who are now being butchered in their hundreds by fascist shrapnel fly the red banner, the righteous course of action is through deliberation in the high councils and courts so that peace may reign and the fascist powers of the day can take rest and wait to triumph for another time. The victory of Mizrahel is the triumph of fascism and the destruction of an entire nationality, the corporatization of an entire state into totalitarian despotism, with all the purposes of its existence reliant upon its monopolization over the identity of the Jewish nation.

If, even when faced with the evil of this future, the Baladullahans remain obstinate in their criticism of the resistance that seeks merely to survive, what more can we expect of their use as an instrument of rationality?

This, unfortunately, is the fate of all liberal democracies. They degenerate and deform until they are reduced to peaceable, impressionable, and malfeasant surrenders in the face of great evil. They deride the militancy of communism and say that it is prideful, arrogant, presumptive, and violent. Communism to them is a burglar or a wandering vagrant shattering windows in the dark of the night. They never think of it as liberation, for their liberation is done in lethargy. 

Where were the Baladullahans when the Mizrahelis began this fascistic, imperialist, ethnonationalist, perhaps genocidal war of annihilation? Certainly, it is not there in the heart of darkness, but in the luxury of their self-importance.

Our volunteers shall continue to arrive on Thyven's fair shores in defense of mankind.
